notes.reason: The sentence is the author's own, but he defines the target of his post before he writes it: "different people mean different things by natural law theory... That is emphatically NOT how it's being used here", and he then stipulates the version he is attacking, whose first pillar is "Morality is solely concerned with one's own happiness." He is arguing against Brian Besong's traditional Thomistic version, and in his follow-up post Besong himself "admits that the view is egoistic". So the note answers a definition the author openly stipulated rather than a factual error. The author also pre-empts this exact objection inside the same post: "Edit: some commenters have said that NLT isn't really egoistic-it's about your 'flourishing' not just happiness. Sure, but it still seems like you should take a hit to your flourishing for the sake of others." The note's own reasoning does not hold either: that Finnis lists several basic goods as valuable for their own sake does not show the theory is non-egoistic, because an egoist can hold an objective list of several things that are intrinsically good for him, which is precisely the reply the author gives elsewhere. The source quotes are accurate to the pages, but the Aquinas source is a devotional piece on Word on Fire, a Catholic apologetics site, which is far too weak to settle a contested question of how to read Aquinas. A philosophy PhD student who has debated this topic will read this as a commenter's objection dressed up as a correction, which is close to what Andy Masley complained about.
